questions.prompt: Computer programs, known as _____, are instructions to the computer.
questions.explanation: The course says: computer programs, known as software, are instructions to the computer.

questions.prompt: Without programs, a computer is:
questions.explanation: The course states that without programs, a computer is an empty machine.

questions.prompt: Machine language is:
options: A program that converts source code into machine code
An English-like language that is easy to learn
A set of primitive instructions built into every computer
A language that uses words such as ADD to write instructions
questions.explanation: Machine language is a set of primitive instructions built into every computer, written in binary code.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a machine language instruction to add two numbers?
questions.explanation: The course shows 1101101010011010 as a binary (machine language) instruction to add two numbers.

questions.prompt: Programs written in native machine language are easy to read and modify.
questions.explanation: Programming in machine language is tedious, and the programs are highly difficult to read and modify.

questions.prompt: Which type of language can the computer understand without any translation?
questions.explanation: Machine language is the set of primitive instructions built into every computer. The computer cannot understand assembly language or high-level languages such as Python, so they must be converted into machine code.

questions.prompt: A program called _____ is used to convert assembly language programs into machine code.
questions.explanation: Since the computer cannot understand assembly language, a program called assembler converts it into machine code.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an assembly language instruction?
questions.explanation: The course gives ADD 2, 3, result as an example of assembly code for adding two numbers.

questions.prompt: Which statement about assembly language is correct?
options: It is English-like and easy to learn
It is translated by an interpreter one statement at a time
The computer understands it directly without translation
It is easier than machine language, but writing code in it is still tedious
questions.explanation: Writing assembly code is easier than machine language, but it is still tedious; an assembler translates it.

questions.prompt: The computer can directly understand and execute assembly language without any translation.
questions.explanation: The computer cannot understand assembly language, so an assembler converts it into machine code.

questions.prompt: Which program converts the assembly instruction ADD 2, 3, result into machine code?
questions.explanation: ADD 2, 3, result is assembly code, and "a program called assembler is used to convert assembly language programs into machine code".

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE about an assembler?
options: It translates high-level source code one statement at a time
It converts assembly language programs into machine code
It translates the entire high-level source code into a machine-code file
It is a set of primitive instructions built into every computer
questions.explanation: "A program called assembler is used to convert assembly language programs into machine code." The other options describe an interpreter, a compiler, and machine language.

questions.prompt: An assembler is used to convert high-level language programs into machine code.
questions.explanation: An assembler converts assembly language programs into machine code. High-level language programs are converted by an interpreter or a compiler.

questions.prompt: The instruction area = 5 * 5 * 3.1415, which computes the area of a circle with radius 5, is an example of:
questions.explanation: The course gives this as a high-level language statement (instruction).

questions.prompt: Because the computer cannot understand high-level languages, a program called an interpreter or a compiler is used to convert them into machine code.
questions.explanation: "Since the computer cannot understand high-level languages, however, a program called interpreter or compiler is used to convert high-level language programs into machine code."

questions.title: Match each language level with its description

pairs.right: Primitive binary instructions built into every computer
Uses instructions like ADD 2, 3, result and needs an assembler
English-like, easy to learn, translated by an interpreter or compiler

questions.prompt: Which program can convert the high-level statement area = 5 * 5 * 3.1415 into machine code?
options: No program is needed; the computer understands it directly
questions.explanation: "Since the computer cannot understand high-level languages, a program called interpreter or compiler is used to convert high-level language programs into machine code."

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE when comparing an assembler with an interpreter and a compiler?
options: An assembler translates high-level languages, while interpreters and compilers translate assembly language
An assembler, an interpreter, and a compiler all translate the entire source code before executing any of it
An assembler translates assembly language, while interpreters and compilers translate high-level languages
An assembler is needed to run high-level languages such as Python
questions.explanation: An assembler converts assembly language programs into machine code; an interpreter or compiler converts high-level language programs into machine code. Option B is false because an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.

questions.prompt: Which type of programming language is English-like and easy to learn and program?
questions.explanation: "The high-level languages are English-like and easy to learn and program." Machine language is binary code, and assembly language is still tedious to write.

questions.title: Match each popular high-level language with its description

pairs.right: Developed for the Department of Defense
Common Business Oriented Language, used for business applications
Developed by Sun Microsystems for platform-independent Internet applications
Simple, structured language primarily for teaching programming
An object-oriented language based on C
Microsoft language to rapidly develop Windows-based applications

questions.prompt: The instructions in a high-level programming language are called:
questions.explanation: The course says the instructions in a high-level programming language are called statements.

questions.prompt: A program written in a high-level language is called a:
questions.explanation: A program written in a high-level language is called a source program or source code.

questions.prompt: How does an interpreter translate a program?
options: It translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed
It manages and controls the computer's activities
It converts assembly language programs into machine code
It reads one statement, translates it to machine code or virtual machine code, and executes it right away
questions.explanation: An interpreter reads one statement from the source code, translates it, and then executes it right away.

questions.prompt: One statement from the source code may be translated into:
questions.explanation: The course notes that a statement from the source code may be translated into several machine instructions.

questions.prompt: An interpreter translates the entire source code into a machine-code file before executing it.
questions.explanation: That describes a compiler; an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.

questions.prompt: _____ reads one statement from the source code, translates it to machine code or virtual machine code, and then executes it right away.
questions.explanation: This is the definition of an interpreter. A compiler first translates the entire source code into a machine-code file.

questions.prompt: An interpreter translates one statement into machine code or virtual machine code and then executes it right away.
questions.explanation: "An interpreter reads one statement from the source code, translates it to the machine code or virtual machine code, and then executes it right away."

questions.prompt: How does a compiler translate a program?
options: It translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, and the machine-code file is then executed
It reads and executes one statement at a time right away
It converts assembly language programs into machine code
It runs the software on many data sets to check performance
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed.

questions.prompt: The main difference between an interpreter and a compiler is that:
options: A compiler translates assembly language, while an interpreter translates high-level language
An interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time, while a compiler translates the entire source code into a machine-code file that is then executed
An interpreter produces a machine-code file, while a compiler executes each statement right away
Only a compiler can translate high-level language programs into machine code
questions.explanation: An interpreter "reads one statement ... Translates it ... And then executes it right away"; a compiler "translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, and the machine-code file is then executed". Both translate high-level languages; assembly language is translated by an assembler.

questions.prompt: A compiler translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed.
questions.explanation: This is the definition of compiling source code.

questions.title: Compare between an Assembler, an Interpreter, and a Compiler. Match each tool with how it translates.

pairs.right: Converts assembly language programs into machine code
Translates one statement of the high-level source code and executes it right away
Translates the entire high-level source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed

questions.explanation: Assembler: assembly language to machine code. Interpreter: one statement translated, then executed right away. Compiler: the whole source code becomes a machine-code file that is then executed.

questions.prompt: _____ translates the entire high-level source code into a machine-code file, and the machine-code file is then executed.
questions.explanation: This is the definition of a compiler. An interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time; an assembler converts assembly language (not high-level source code) into machine code.

questions.prompt: A compiler executes each statement right away after translating it, without producing a machine-code file.
questions.explanation: That describes an interpreter. A compiler translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, and the machine-code file is then executed.

questions.title: Compare an Assembler, an Interpreter, and a Compiler. Match each point with the correct answer.

pairs.right: Assembly language

pairs.left: Language translated by an interpreter or a compiler
pairs.right: High-level language (source code)

pairs.left: How much an interpreter translates before executing
pairs.right: One statement at a time

pairs.left: How much a compiler translates before executing
pairs.right: The entire source code
A machine-code file that is then executed

questions.explanation: Assembler: assembly language to machine code. Interpreter: reads one statement, translates it, executes it right away. Compiler: translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed.

questions.prompt: The operating system (OS) is:
options: A program that converts assembly code into machine code
The hardware that executes machine instructions
A program that manages and controls a computer's activities
An application program such as a word processor
questions.explanation: The operating system (OS) is a program that manages and controls a computer's activities.

questions.prompt: In the layers User, Application Programs, Operating System, Hardware, which layer lies directly between the application programs and the hardware?
questions.explanation: The diagram shows User -> Application Programs -> Operating System -> Hardware.

questions.prompt: Application programs such as an Internet browser and a word processor can run without an operating system.
questions.explanation: The course says application programs cannot run without an operating system.

questions.title: Match each Python property with its meaning

pairs.right: Can be used to write code for any programming tasks
Translated and executed one statement at a time
Data are objects created from classes
Users may study, change, and distribute the software

questions.prompt: Python is an interpreted language. This means Python code is:
options: Translated and executed one statement at a time by an interpreter
Compiled entirely and then executed altogether
Converted into assembly code by an assembler
questions.explanation: Python code is translated and executed one statement at a time by an interpreter.

questions.prompt: In a compiled language, the entire source code is compiled and then executed altogether.
questions.explanation: The course contrasts Python (interpreted) with compiled languages, where the entire source code is compiled then executed.

questions.prompt: Python is a compiled language: its entire source code is compiled and then executed altogether.
questions.explanation: Python is interpreted: its code is translated and executed one statement at a time by an interpreter. Compiling the entire source code and then executing it altogether describes a compiled language.

questions.prompt: A class is essentially:
options: A layer between the application programs and the hardware
A machine-code file produced by a compiler
A single statement in a high-level language
A type that defines objects of the same kind with properties and methods for manipulating them
questions.explanation: A class is a type that defines the objects of the same kind with properties and methods for manipulating objects.

questions.prompt: Object-oriented programming is described as a powerful tool for:
options: Translating the whole program at once
questions.explanation: Object-oriented programming is a powerful tool for developing reusable software.

questions.prompt: Python was created by:
questions.explanation: Python is created by Guido van Rossum in Netherlands in 1990.

questions.prompt: Open-source software is software whose source code is released under a license that:
options: Allows only the copyright holder to change the software
Lets users run the program but never see the source code
Grants users the rights to study, change, and distribute the software to anyone and for any purpose
Only works with the operating system it was written for
questions.explanation: Open-source software releases source code under a license granting users the rights to study, change, and distribute it.

questions.prompt: Which command works on Python 3?
questions.explanation: Print "Hello World" works only on Python 2; on Python 3 you write print("Hello World").

questions.prompt: Python 3 is not backward compatible with Python 2. This means:
options: Python 3 is an older version than Python 2
Python 3 programs must be compiled instead of interpreted
A program written using Python 2 may not work on Python 3
A program written using Python 3 always works on Python 2
questions.explanation: Python 3 is newer but not backward compatible, so a Python 2 program may not work on Python 3.

questions.prompt: The software development life cycle (SDLC) is:
options: The process required to create large-scale software projects
A program that translates source code into machine code
A tool that provides a program editor and debugger
A test suite used to check correctness
questions.explanation: The SDLC is the process required to create large-scale software projects.

questions.prompt: What percentage of time in the SDLC is spent on problem specification and program design?
questions.explanation: The course says 25 to 40 percent of time is spent on problem specification and program design.

questions.prompt: In the SDLC, 40 to 65 percent of the time is spent on:
options: Reviewing, modifying, fixing, and improving software
questions.explanation: 40 to 65 percent of time is spent reviewing, modifying, fixing, and improving software.

questions.prompt: In the SDLC, initial implementation takes the largest share of time (40 to 65 percent).
questions.explanation: Initial implementation takes only 10 to 20 percent; 40 to 65 percent goes to reviewing, modifying, fixing, and improving software.

questions.prompt: The SDLC steps are grouped into which three stages?
questions.explanation: The SDLC steps are listed under 1. Before Implementation, 2. Implementation, 3. After Implementation.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order of the 'Before Implementation' steps?
options: Problem specification, feasibility study, algorithm selection/analysis, program design
Program design, feasibility study, problem specification, algorithm selection/analysis
Feasibility study, problem specification, program design, algorithm selection/analysis
Feasibility study, program design, problem specification, coding
questions.explanation: The course lists a. Feasibility study, b. Problem specification, c. Program design, d. Algorithm selection or development, and analysis.

questions.prompt: Coding and debugging are part of the Implementation stage of the SDLC.
questions.explanation: Implementation: a. Coding, b. Debugging.

questions.prompt: Which of the following belongs to the 'After Implementation' stage of the SDLC?
questions.explanation: After Implementation includes testing/verification/benchmarking, documentation, and maintenance.

questions.prompt: In the SDLC steps, Documentation is listed under the 'Before Implementation' stage.
questions.explanation: Documentation is listed under After Implementation, with testing and maintenance.

questions.prompt: Which SDLC step evaluates the costs and benefits of various solutions and considers alternatives?
questions.explanation: Feasibility study: evaluate the costs and benefits of various solutions; consider alternatives.

questions.prompt: A clear statement of the problem the software is to solve is produced in which step?
questions.explanation: Problem specification: clear statement of the problem the software is to solve; a problem specification document is prepared.

questions.prompt: Breaking the problem into tasks and subtasks using divide-and-conquer (top-down decomposition) happens in which step?
questions.explanation: Program design: break the problem into tasks and subtasks; divide-and-conquer, top-down decomposition.

questions.prompt: In the 'Algorithm selection or development, and analysis' step, the programmer:
options: Translates the pseudocode into computer code
Chooses or designs an algorithm for each subtask and analyzes its efficiency
Evaluates the costs and benefits of various solutions
questions.explanation: This step: choose or design an algorithm for each subtask; analyze efficiency.

questions.title: Match each SDLC step with the document it produces

pairs.right: Problem specification document
Program design document
Pseudocode with efficiency analysis and rationale
Program code document

questions.prompt: The coding step means:
options: Translating the pseudocode and design into computer code
Breaking the problem into tasks and subtasks
questions.explanation: Coding: translate the pseudocode and design into computer code.

questions.prompt: In the coding step of the SDLC: Better design = _____
questions.explanation: The course states: better design = easier coding.

questions.prompt: Debugging is:
options: Proving that the code is correct
Running the software on many data sets
questions.explanation: Debugging: locating and correcting program errors.

questions.prompt: Dividing by zero is an example of which type of error?
questions.explanation: Runtime errors are illegal operations like dividing by zero.

questions.prompt: An error in the algorithm itself that gives wrong results is a:
questions.explanation: Logic errors: errors in the algorithm itself that give wrong results.

questions.prompt: A syntax error is an illegal operation such as dividing by zero.
questions.explanation: Dividing by zero is a runtime error; a syntax error is wrong grammar in code statements.

questions.prompt: Logic errors are errors in the algorithm itself that give wrong results.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of logic errors.

questions.title: Match each type of program error with its description

pairs.right: Wrong grammar in code statements
Illegal operation such as dividing by zero
Error in the algorithm itself that gives wrong results

questions.prompt: Wrong grammar in code statements is a:
questions.explanation: Syntax errors: "wrong grammar in code statements". Runtime errors are illegal operations like dividing by zero; logic errors are errors in the algorithm itself.

questions.prompt: Which type of testing checks how modules work together?
questions.explanation: Integration testing: test how modules work together.

questions.prompt: When a change occurs, testing to be sure the change did not introduce errors is called:
questions.explanation: Regression testing: when a change occurs, test to be sure the change did not introduce errors.

questions.prompt: Running the software on many data sets (inputs) to check if performance meets the required limits is called:
questions.explanation: Benchmarking: run the software on many data sets to check if performance meets the required limits.

questions.prompt: Integration testing tests each module or subtask on its own.
questions.explanation: Testing each module alone is unit testing; integration testing tests how modules work together.

questions.prompt: Regression testing is done when a change occurs, to be sure the change did not introduce errors.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of regression testing.

questions.title: Match each testing activity with its purpose

pairs.right: Develop a test suite to check correctness
Test each module or subtask
Test how modules work together
Make sure a change did not introduce errors
Prove the code is correct
Check performance on many data sets against required limits

questions.prompt: Testing each module or subtask is called:
questions.explanation: Unit testing: "test each module or subtask". Integration testing tests how modules work together.

questions.prompt: Which activity is done to prove that the code is correct?
questions.explanation: Program verification: "to prove code is correct". Empirical testing develops a test suite to check correctness; benchmarking checks performance.

questions.prompt: Empirical testing means developing a test suite to check correctness.
questions.explanation: "Empirical testing: develop a test suite to check correctness."

questions.prompt: External documentation consists of:
options: All earlier documents, such as the problem specification and program design
Only the instructions that help users run programs
questions.explanation: External documentation: all earlier documents (problem specification, program design, etc.).

questions.prompt: Program maintenance includes:
options: Breaking the problem into tasks and subtasks
Adding features, fixing bugs, and improving performance
Evaluating costs and benefits of solutions
questions.explanation: Program maintenance: add features, fix bugs, and improve performance.

questions.prompt: User documentation is information for programmers to understand the code.
questions.explanation: That is technical documentation; user documentation helps users run programs.

questions.title: Match each type of documentation with its description

pairs.right: Comments in code
All earlier documents (problem specification, program design, etc.)
Information for programmers to understand the code
Helps users run programs

questions.prompt: Comments in code are called:
questions.explanation: Internal documentation: "comments in code". External documentation is all the earlier documents (problem specification, program design, etc.).

questions.prompt: IDE stands for:
questions.explanation: Most programmers use an Integrated Development Environment (IDE) for developing software.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT listed among the things an IDE provides?
questions.explanation: The IDE provides a program editor, file manager, compiler or interpreter, debugger, prototypes, rapid prototyping, and version control and document management.

questions.prompt: The two models for the software development process presented in the course are:
questions.explanation: There are two models for the software development process: 1. Waterfall model, 2. Agile model.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the Waterfall model?
options: The process is sequential; one step must be completed before the next, and previous steps are never revisited
The customer or user is involved throughout the process
Problem specification can change at any time
It is a flexible and iterative approach
questions.explanation: Waterfall: sequential; one step completed before moving on; previous steps never revisited.

questions.prompt: In the Waterfall model, previous steps can be revisited whenever needed.
questions.explanation: In the Waterfall model the process is sequential and the previous steps are never revisited.

questions.prompt: In which model is the software development process sequential?
questions.explanation: Waterfall model: "The software development process is sequential." The Agile model is a flexible and iterative approach.

questions.prompt: In which model are the previous steps never revisited?
questions.explanation: Waterfall model: "One step must be completed before moving on to the next. The previous steps are never revisited." Agile is iterative and expects changes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Waterfall model?
options: The software development process is sequential
One step must be completed before moving on to the next
It is a flexible and iterative approach
The previous steps are never revisited
questions.explanation: Options A, B and D are the three Waterfall points on the course. "A flexible and iterative approach" describes the Agile model.

questions.prompt: In the Waterfall model, one step must be completed before moving on to the next.
questions.explanation: Waterfall model: the process is sequential; "one step must be completed before moving on to the next" and previous steps are never revisited.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order of the phases in the Waterfall model?
options: Requirements, Design, Analysis, Coding/implementation, Testing, Operation/deployment, Maintenance
Analysis, Requirements, Design, Coding/implementation, Operation/deployment, Testing, Maintenance
Requirements, Analysis, Design, Coding/implementation, Testing, Operation/deployment, Maintenance
Requirements, Analysis, Coding/implementation, Design, Testing, Maintenance, Operation/deployment
questions.explanation: The Waterfall diagram goes down step by step: Requirements, Analysis, Design, Coding/implementation, Testing, Operation/deployment, Maintenance. Each step is completed before the next one starts.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the Agile model?
options: One step must be completed before moving on to the next
The previous steps are never revisited
It is a flexible and iterative approach in which changes are expected
questions.explanation: Agile: a flexible and iterative approach; changes are expected; respond in an agile way.

questions.prompt: In which model is the customer or user involved throughout the process?
questions.explanation: Involving the customer or user throughout the process is part of the Agile philosophy.

questions.prompt: How does the Agile model differ from the Waterfall model?
options: Agile expects changes and keeps the user involved, while Waterfall completes each step in sequence without going back
Agile is sequential, while Waterfall is flexible and iterative
Agile has no testing, while Waterfall has no design
Agile never revisits previous steps, while Waterfall does
questions.explanation: Waterfall is sequential with no revisiting; Agile is flexible and iterative, expects changes, and involves the customer throughout.

questions.prompt: In the Agile model, the problem specification is fixed and cannot change once written.
questions.explanation: Agile philosophy: problem specification can change at any time; changes are expected.

questions.prompt: The Agile model is presented as an alternative to the Waterfall model.
questions.explanation: The course says Agile is an alternative to the waterfall model.

questions.prompt: In the Agile model, the customer or user is involved only at the beginning of the process.
questions.explanation: Agile philosophy: the customer or user is involved throughout the process.

questions.prompt: Which model is a flexible and iterative approach?
questions.explanation: Agile model: "It is a flexible and iterative approach", an alternative to the waterfall model, which is sequential.

questions.prompt: In which model can the problem specification change at any time?
questions.explanation: Agile philosophy: "Problem specification can change at any time; changes are expected." Waterfall is sequential and never revisits previous steps.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT part of the Agile model's philosophy?
options: Problem specification can change at any time
Changes are expected; respond in an agile way
Customer or user is involved throughout the process
The previous steps are never revisited
questions.explanation: The three points of the Agile philosophy are options A, B and C. "The previous steps are never revisited" describes the Waterfall model.

questions.prompt: In the Agile model, changes are expected and the team responds to them in an agile way.
questions.explanation: Agile philosophy: "Changes are expected; respond in an agile way."

questions.title: Compare the Waterfall Model and the Agile Model. Match each point with the correct description.

pairs.right: Sequential; one step must be completed before moving on to the next
Never revisited
Flexible and iterative
Can change at any time
Involved throughout the process

questions.explanation: Waterfall: sequential, one step completed before the next, previous steps never revisited. Agile: flexible and iterative alternative to waterfall; problem specification can change at any time, changes are expected, customer or user involved throughout.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the phases shown in the Agile Model cycle diagram?
questions.explanation: The Agile cycle shows Requirements feeding a loop of Design, Develop, Test, Deploy, and Review.

questions.prompt: According to the summary, the Software Development Life Cycle is critical in developing and documenting a software product.
questions.explanation: This is stated in the course summary.

questions.prompt: The Waterfall model and the Agile model have the same philosophy.
questions.explanation: Course summary: "The Waterfall model and Agile models have different philosophies." Waterfall is sequential; Agile is flexible and iterative and expects changes.
